prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Houston, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1213; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you describe where you were driving and what happened at the time of the collision?

A: I was heading east on a main road in Houston, in the right lane. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I came to a complete stop at a light. A few seconds later I felt a hard jolt from behind.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No. I was looking forward at the light and didn't see it coming. I checked my mirror after, and the other car was right up against my bumper.

Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle afterward?

A: Yes, I got out, but my neck and right shoulder were really sore right away. I sat on the curb until the police arrived.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They took X-rays and told me I had a strained shoulder muscle. I was given a sling and some pain medication.

Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limited movement?

A: Yes. Lifting anything above my head is difficult, and I've had trouble sleeping on my right side. I'm scheduled to see a physical therapist next week.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: I've been out for a few days, and I'm working with my employer on modified duties for the time being.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident or your injuries?

A: Just that I was following the rules of the road and stopped properly. I want this to be handled fairly.

Q: Understood. Thank you for your time. We'll be in touch with next steps.

A: Thank you.
